demos.raw_question:
Analyze the 5G wireless network drive-test user plane data and engineering parameters.
Identify the reason for the throughput dropping below 600Mbps in certain road sections.
From the following 8 potential root causes, select the most likely one and enclose its number in \boxed{{}} in the final answer.

C1: The serving cell's downtilt angle is too large, causing weak coverage at the far end.
C2: The serving cell's coverage distance exceeds 1km, resulting in over-shooting.
C3: A neighboring cell provides higher throughput.
C4: Non-colocated co-frequency neighboring cells cause severe overlapping coverage.
C5: Frequent handovers degrade performance.
C6: Neighbor cell and serving cell have the same PCI mod 30, leading to interference.
C7: Test vehicle speed exceeds 40km/h, impacting user throughput.
C8: Average scheduled RBs are below 160, affecting throughput.

Given:
- The default electronic downtilt value is 255, representing a downtilt angle of 6 degrees. Other values represent the actual downtilt angle in degrees.

Beam Scenario and Vertical Beamwidth Relationships:
- When the cell's Beam Scenario is set to Default or SCENARIO_1 to SCENARIO_5, the vertical beamwidth is 6 degrees.
- When the cell's Beam Scenario is set to SCENARIO_6 to SCENARIO_11, the vertical beamwidth is 12 degrees.
- When the cell's Beam Scenario is set to SCENARIO_12 or above, the vertical beamwidth is 25 degrees.

signature.instructions:
Diagnose one TeleLogs case by iteratively requesting label-neutral measurements.

The tools return deterministic measurements parsed from the raw drive-test and
engineering tables; they never return a diagnosis. Every number in the final
reasoning must come from a tool observation of this case; quoting a value that
no tool returned, or describing a measurement as unavailable without the
observation saying so, is an error. Comparisons must be written as signed
inequalities between the two numbers, never as words like "worse", "weaker" or
"better"; remember that for negative numbers -2.1 > -3 and -95 < -90.

Stage one. First call exactly these four tools, one call each:
analyze_throughput_segments, analyze_coverage_geometry, analyze_mobility, and
analyze_radio_resources. Then verify the four decisive criteria, one line per
criterion. Each line must quote the named observation field, write the two
numbers joined by < or >, and state the verdict: "triggered" when the stated
condition is true, "not triggered" when it is false.
- C2: triggered when maximum_distance_km (analyze_coverage_geometry) is
  greater than 1;
- C5: triggered when transition_count (analyze_mobility) is 3 or more; a count
  of exactly 3 already triggers;
- C7: triggered when maximum_speed_kmh (analyze_mobility) is greater than 40;
- C8: triggered when low_throughput_rows_mean_scheduled_rbs
  (analyze_radio_resources) is below 160.
A triggered criterion IS the diagnosis. Stop at the first triggered line: do
not call any further tool, do not discuss other causes, answer that class with
the four verification lines as the reasoning. Writing a measured value whose
comparison makes a criterion true and then labelling it "not triggered", or
selecting a different class after a triggered line, is an error. No
qualitative narrative can override a verified decisive criterion.

Stage two, only when all four verdicts are "not triggered". Check the
sufficient witness for C1: a row listed in rows_below_main_lobe_lower_edge
(analyze_coverage_geometry) whose throughput is below the stated criterion AND
whose serving RSRP satisfies RSRP <= -90 proves C1; write the signed
inequality (-93.1 < -90 satisfies it; -88.9 > -90 does not). If no row
qualifies, call analyze_pci_relations and analyze_neighbor_overlap, one call
each; writing any residual conclusion without both observations is an error.
Then check these rules one at a time, in this exact order, quoting the named
observation field:
1. minimum_difference_mbps from segment_minimum_comparison
   (analyze_throughput_segments) of at least 142.5 selects C3; undefined when
   the drive has a single segment;
2. otherwise a non-empty equal_residue_pairs from analyze_pci_relations
   selects C6;
3. otherwise a best_noncolocated_gap from analyze_neighbor_overlap of -3 dB or
   stronger, meaning gap > -3 or gap = -3, selects C4 (null means no
   non-colocated neighbor);
4. otherwise a low-throughput row listed in rows_below_main_lobe_lower_edge
   selects C1;
5. otherwise select C3.
Exactly as in stage one, stop at the first satisfied rule: it is the
diagnosis, and later rules must not be evaluated or mentioned. Selecting a
class whose rule comes after the first satisfied rule is an error. This order
is a calibrated tie-break over the quoted measurements only; it never replaces
measuring. Close by citing the decisive rows and values and select exactly one
class.

You are an Agent. In each episode, you will be given the fields `raw_question` as input. And you can see your past trajectory so far.
Your goal is to use one or more of the supplied tools to collect any necessary information for producing `reasoning`, `answer`.

To do this, you will interleave next_thought, next_tool_name, and next_tool_args in each turn, and also when finishing the task.
After each tool call, you receive a resulting observation, which gets appended to your trajectory.

When writing next_thought, you may reason about the current situation and plan for future steps.
When selecting the next_tool_name and its next_tool_args, the tool must be one of:

(1) analyze_throughput_segments, whose description is <desc>Summarize throughput by serving segment and list low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(2) analyze_coverage_geometry, whose description is <desc>Measure serving distance, antenna vertical geometry, and serving RSRP by row. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(3) analyze_mobility, whose description is <desc>Measure vehicle speed and serving-cell transition events. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(4) analyze_radio_resources, whose description is <desc>Measure scheduled resource blocks overall and on low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(5) analyze_neighbor_overlap, whose description is <desc>Measure non-colocated neighbor power relative to serving power on low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(6) analyze_pci_relations, whose description is <desc>Inspect serving and neighbor PCI modulo-30 residues on low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(7) finish, whose description is <desc>Marks the task as complete. That is, signals that all information for producing the outputs, i.e. `reasoning`, `answer`, are now available to be extracted.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
When providing `next_tool_args`, the value inside the field must be in JSON format

demos.raw_question:
Analyze the 5G wireless network drive-test user plane data and engineering parameters.
Identify the reason for the throughput dropping below 600Mbps in certain road sections.
From the following 8 potential root causes, select the most likely one and enclose its number in \boxed{{}} in the final answer.

C1: The serving cell's downtilt angle is too large, causing weak coverage at the far end.
C2: The serving cell's coverage distance exceeds 1km, resulting in over-shooting.
C3: A neighboring cell provides higher throughput.
C4: Non-colocated co-frequency neighboring cells cause severe overlapping coverage.
C5: Frequent handovers degrade performance.
C6: Neighbor cell and serving cell have the same PCI mod 30, leading to interference.
C7: Test vehicle speed exceeds 40km/h, impacting user throughput.
C8: Average scheduled RBs are below 160, affecting throughput.

Given:
- The default electronic downtilt value is 255, representing a downtilt angle of 6 degrees. Other values represent the actual downtilt angle in degrees.

- When the cell's Beam Scenario is set to Default or SCENARIO_1 to SCENARIO_5, the vertical beamwidth is 6 degrees.
- When the cell's Beam Scenario is set to SCENARIO_6 to SCENARIO_11, the vertical beamwidth is 12 degrees.
- When the cell's Beam Scenario is set to SCENARIO_12 or above, the vertical beamwidth is 25 degrees.

signature.instructions:
Diagnose one TeleLogs case by iteratively requesting label-neutral measurements.

The tools return deterministic measurements parsed from the raw drive-test and
engineering tables; they never return a diagnosis. Every number in the final
reasoning must come from a tool observation of this case; quoting a value that
no tool returned, or describing a measurement as unavailable without the
observation saying so, is an error. Comparisons must be written as signed
inequalities between the two numbers, never as words like "worse", "weaker" or
"better"; remember that for negative numbers -2.1 > -3 and -95 < -90.

Stage one. First call exactly these four tools, one call each:
analyze_throughput_segments, analyze_coverage_geometry, analyze_mobility, and
analyze_radio_resources. Then verify the four decisive criteria, one line per
criterion. Each line must quote the named observation field, write the two
numbers joined by < or >, and state the verdict: "triggered" when the stated
condition is true, "not triggered" when it is false.
- C2: triggered when maximum_distance_km (analyze_coverage_geometry) is
  greater than 1;
- C5: triggered when transition_count (analyze_mobility) is 3 or more; a count
  of exactly 3 already triggers;
- C7: triggered when maximum_speed_kmh (analyze_mobility) is greater than 40;
- C8: triggered when low_throughput_rows_mean_scheduled_rbs
  (analyze_radio_resources) is below 160.
A triggered criterion IS the diagnosis. Stop at the first triggered line: do
not call any further tool, do not discuss other causes, answer that class with
the four verification lines as the reasoning. Writing a measured value whose
comparison makes a criterion true and then labelling it "not triggered", or
selecting a different class after a triggered line, is an error. No
qualitative narrative can override a verified decisive criterion.

Stage two, only when all four verdicts are "not triggered". Check the
sufficient witness for C1: a row listed in rows_below_main_lobe_lower_edge
(analyze_coverage_geometry) whose throughput is below the stated criterion AND
whose serving RSRP satisfies RSRP <= -90 proves C1; write the signed
inequality (-93.1 < -90 satisfies it; -88.9 > -90 does not). If no row
qualifies, call analyze_pci_relations and analyze_neighbor_overlap, one call
each; writing any residual conclusion without both observations is an error.
Then check these rules one at a time, in this exact order, quoting the named
observation field:
1. minimum_difference_mbps from segment_minimum_comparison
   (analyze_throughput_segments) of at least 142.5 selects C3; undefined when
   the drive has a single segment;
2. otherwise a non-empty equal_residue_pairs from analyze_pci_relations
   selects C6;
3. otherwise a best_noncolocated_gap from analyze_neighbor_overlap of -3 dB or
   stronger, meaning gap > -3 or gap = -3, selects C4 (null means no
   non-colocated neighbor);
4. otherwise a low-throughput row listed in rows_below_main_lobe_lower_edge
   selects C1;
5. otherwise select C3.
Exactly as in stage one, stop at the first satisfied rule: it is the
diagnosis, and later rules must not be evaluated or mentioned. Selecting a
class whose rule comes after the first satisfied rule is an error. This order
is a calibrated tie-break over the quoted measurements only; it never replaces
measuring. Close by citing the decisive rows and values and select exactly one
class.

fields.description: Auditable diagnosis citing tool measurements and row evidence, at most 180 words.
Exactly one class identifier: C1,C2,C3,C4,C5,C6,C7,or C8.
